result.title: From Visual Matching to Textual Conditioning: Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation via Reference Inversion
result.summary: Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation (CD-FSS) aims to segment objects from unseen domains using only a few annotated references. Recent Segment Anything Model (SAM)-based methods have advanced CD-FSS, yet their reference-target visual matching is highly sensitive to target appearance variations. SAM3 introduces text-conditioned segmentation, enabling natural-language descriptions to guide segmentation across target images, but directly using the category name as the condition still yields unstable performance under severe domain shifts. We propose Reference Inversion for SAM3 (RI-SAM3) that leverages SAM3's large-scale vision-language pre-training to learn suitable textual tokens for each target category. RI-SAM3 comprises three core designs: (i) Bi-level Reference Inversion that learns complementary tokens before and after the frozen text encoder: the former remain anchored in SAM3's text space while the latter represent the category more flexibly; (ii) Layer-adaptive Textual Conditioning combines these tokens differently as object queries evolve across decoder layers; and (iii) Presence-aware Confidence Supervision that jointly supervises query confidence and target presence for reliable predictions. With SAM3 frozen, RI-SAM3 optimizes around 12K parameters only per category and it efficiently segments each target in a single forward pass with reusable textual conditioning without per-sample reference-target visual matching. Extensive experiments over multiple widely adopted benchmarks show that RI-SAM3 achieves superior performance consistently in CD-FSS tasks, together with strong robustness, efficiency, and generalization.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 RI-SAM3，在冻结 SAM3 的前提下为每个目标类别学习约 12K 参数的文本 token，通过编码器前后的双层参考反转、随解码层变化的文本条件，以及联合监督查询置信与目标存在性的机制，用可复用的文本条件替代逐样本视觉匹配来完成跨域少样本分割。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将参考信息压缩为可跨解码层复用的条件 token，以及 presence 置信监督，可能为「视觉证据如何转为内部条件状态」和停止/弃答判断提供可供核查的线索，但该工作面向分割、无多步 latent 推理过程，迁移性需进一步判断。
